title: Movie ticket booking design
idea: A ticket booking design models cinemas, screens, shows and seats, and adds a short-lived seat hold so one seat is never booked twice.

analogy.text: A shop assistant puts a jacket behind the counter for you for ten minutes. Others cannot buy it unless you fail to return in time.
analogy.breaks: Thousands of buyers can grab one seat in the same instant.

points: A `Show` is one movie on one `Screen`, with its own seats and `Booking`s.
Each show seat moves free, held, booked; an expired hold frees it.
Check and claim must happen together, with no `await` between them.
Across servers, the database enforces the claim, for example with a unique key.

steps.caption: The show opens for sale. Every seat starts free.
Ana picks C7. The hold is written at once, before any payment starts.
Ben also picks C7. The hold already exists, so his request is refused immediately.
Ana's payment succeeds while her hold is still valid. C7 becomes booked.
Cy holds D1, but his payment takes longer than the hold allows.
The hold expires. D1 is free again, and Cy's late payment must be refunded.
Dev holds D1 and pays in time. No seat was ever sold twice.

code.title: The double-booking bug
code.caption: Node runs one request at a time, yet both buyers win. The gap is the `await` between check and write.

walk.text: Both requests check the seat while it is still free.
Each pauses for payment, letting the other request run its check.
Both write the seat. The last writer silently overwrites the first.
Two concurrent requests for C7, then the final owner.

code.title: Seat holds with expiry
code.caption: A fake clock makes expiry repeatable. Change the hold length from 5 to 10 minutes and rerun.

walk.text: `hold` checks and claims in one synchronous step, so no other request can slip between.
`owns` is true only for the holder, and only before the hold expires.
A seat already booked or held by someone else is refused before payment.
After paying, re-check the hold. An expired hold means the seat may be gone.
Confirm the booking, then release the hold it no longer needs.
The clock and payment are injected, so the run is deterministic.

pitfalls: Never put an `await` between checking a seat and claiming it.
An in-memory lock protects one process only; use the database for many servers.
Re-check the hold after payment, and refund if it expired.

quiz.why: Both calls run their check before either resumes from `await`. Each sees the seat free, so both return `ok`.

takeaway: Hold first, pay second, re-check the hold, then book.

starters: How would I enforce seat holds in SQL across many servers?
Should holds use optimistic or pessimistic locking?
How do I model seat categories and pricing per show?
